claim.why_it_matters: In GR 11's TIME table (ACCEPT statement) the sub-items a) and b) belong inside the 5-6 row's Contents cell, but the transcription closes the table after that row and sets them as free paragraphs. The 7-8 row then falls out of the table as an indented text line. All the words are kept, but the table no longer shows that a) and b) qualify positions 5-6, and position 7-8 is no longer a table row.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 411 (PDF p433), ACCEPT GR 11: the TIME table shows 5-6 '...seconds past the minute in the range:' with a) and b) indented under its Contents column, then 7-8 '...hundredths of a second ... 00 through 99. 00 is returned if ...'. The markdown carries every word in the same order: the 5-6 row ends with 'in the range:' and is immediately followed by a) and b), then '7-8 Two numeric characters of the hundredths ... 00 through 99. 00 is returned ...'. The colon ending the 5-6 cell binds a) and b) to it unambiguously (no other row precedes them and they complete its sentence), and the 7-8 line still states its positions and contents. The difference is table layout only (markdown tables cannot hold a nested list in a cell); no text is missing, misattributed or reworded, so the meaning is unchanged. By the verification criteria (formatting-only, meaning unchanged) the claim is refuted.
